Small-class effects in 79 schools of Project STAR

Source: R/data.R
star_schools.Rd

School-specific estimates of the effect of small classes on achievement in kindergarten, from Tennessee's Student Teacher Achievement Ratio (STAR) project. Within each of 79 schools, students and teachers were assigned at random to small classes or to regular classes, the regular ones with or without a teacher's aide, so the experiment is a multisite trial with the schools as its sites. The estimate of a school is the difference between its small classes and its regular classes of either kind on a composite of the kindergarten reading and mathematics scores.

Usage

star_schools

Format

A data frame with 79 rows and 12 columns:

site

Sequential site number, in ascending order of school_id.

school_id

School identifier in the public-use data.

location

Kind of area that the school serves: "inner city", "suburban", "rural" or "urban".

yi

Estimate of the effect of small classes: small minus regular, in standard deviations of the composite score.

sei

Standard error of yi, from the model with a random intercept for each class.

vi

Sampling variance, sei^2.

yi_ols, sei_ols

The same contrast and its standard error by ordinary least squares within the school.

n_students, n_students_small

Numbers of students with both scores: in the school, and in its small classes.

n_classes, n_classes_small

Numbers of classes: in the school, and small ones.

Source

Achilles, C. M., Bain, H. P., Bellott, F., Boyd-Zaharias, J., Finn, J., Folger, J., Johnston, J. and Word, E. (2008). Tennessee's Student Teacher Achievement Ratio (STAR) project. Harvard Dataverse, V1. doi:10.7910/DVN/SIWH9F . The data are released under CC0 1.0. The experiment is described in Finn, J. D. and Achilles, C. M. (1990). Answers and questions about class size: A statewide experiment. American Educational Research Journal, 27(3), 557-577. doi:10.3102/00028312027003557 . data-raw/star.R in the source repository builds the estimates from the student file STAR_Students.tab, and the attribute source of the data frame records the file, the sample and the model.

Details

The outcome is the mean of the standardized reading and mathematics scale scores of the Stanford Achievement Test, standardized again, so the estimates are in standard deviations of that composite. Of the 6,325 students in kindergarten, the 5,786 with both scores are used; they sat in 325 classes, 127 of them small.

The estimates and their standard errors come from one linear mixed model fitted to all the schools by restricted maximum likelihood. The model has an intercept and a small-class contrast for each school and a random intercept for each class. The variance of the class intercepts is taken to be the same for small and for regular classes and in every school, and so is the residual variance, so the standard error of a school depends only on the numbers and the sizes of its small and its regular classes. A school has from one to four small classes, and that number, more than the number of its students, limits how precise its estimate can be.

yi_ols and sei_ols are the same contrast computed within each school by ordinary least squares, with the students of a school taken as independent. That ignores what the students of a class have in common, and the standard error is smaller for every school. The two columns are there to show how much a fit depends on its standard errors; the article "Small classes in 79 schools" on the package website, https://joonho112.github.io/bayesEfron/, fits both, and it also varies the assumption about the variance of the classes.

See also

as_bef_data(), bayes_efron_fit()

Examples

head(star_schools)
#>   site school_id location          yi       sei        vi      yi_ols   sei_ols
#> 1    1    112038    urban -0.22151425 0.4924872 0.2425436 -0.22519182 0.1344110
#> 2    2    123056    rural  0.07580528 0.4930496 0.2430979  0.07736164 0.1712559
#> 3    3    128068    rural -0.02022031 0.4980018 0.2480058 -0.02650660 0.2273065
#> 4    4    128076 suburban  0.05546138 0.4962996 0.2463133  0.05676752 0.1630621
#> 5    5    128079    rural  1.39287138 0.4894715 0.2395823  1.40446846 0.2903351
#> 6    6    130085 suburban  0.15082600 0.3991840 0.1593479  0.14366035 0.1824108
#>   n_students n_students_small n_classes n_classes_small
#> 1         52               15         3               1
#> 2         51               15         3               1
#> 3         54               13         3               1
#> 4         58               13         3               1
#> 5         59               15         3               1
#> 6         71               29         4               2
as_bef_data(star_schools)
#> <bef_data>
#> Sites: 79
#> Source: data.frame
#> theta_hat: min -0.8986; median 0.1459; max 1.393
#> sigma: min 0.2843; median 0.4081; max 0.5684

# The contrast and standard errors that take the students of a school as
# independent.
as_bef_data(star_schools, theta_hat = "yi_ols", sigma = "sei_ols")
#> <bef_data>
#> Sites: 79
#> Source: data.frame
#> theta_hat: min -0.8664; median 0.1437; max 1.404
#> sigma: min 0.1216; median 0.2237; max 0.3945
